metaTitle: Get found on Google and cited by AI | FirstCompile
metaDescription: Technical SEO and GEO: structured data, page speed, crawlability, and pages AI assistants can quote. Shipped as code, one fixed price agreed in writing.
h1: Search visibility is an engineering problem.
intro: Ten years ago, being found meant ranking on Google. Now a growing share of buyers ask ChatGPT or Perplexity instead, and those tools answer with a short written summary and a handful of cited sources. If your site is not one of them, that buyer never sees you. More blog posts rarely fix that. The work is mostly engineering.

Most of what stops a site from ranking, or from being quoted by an AI assistant, is technical. Pages that render only in the browser, so crawlers see an empty shell. Missing structured data. Redirect chains, duplicate URLs, slow responses. We find these problems with a full crawl, fix them in code, and deploy the fixes to your live site with daily written updates on what changed.

The second half is GEO, generative engine optimisation. In practice it means structuring pages so a language model can lift a clean, correct answer with your name attached: standalone answers, schema.org markup, consistent facts about your organisation everywhere they appear. No tricks, because tricks stop working every time the models update.
whoFor: A startup that launched three months ago and gets nothing from search. The product is real, but Google indexed twelve pages and ChatGPT has never heard of you. Usually the site was built without server rendering or structured data, and both are fixable in the codebase you already have.

An established business watching organic traffic slide. Rankings dropped after a redesign or a platform migration, or traffic is flat while buyers move to asking AI assistants. Shopify, WordPress and WooCommerce stores fit here too; themes and plugins create duplicate URLs and slow pages, and both are repairable.
Also anyone about to rebuild a site. Getting crawlability, speed and markup right during the build is far cheaper than retrofitting them after launch.

faq.q: What is GEO and how is it different from SEO?
faq.a: GEO, generative engine optimisation, is the work of getting your site cited by AI assistants like ChatGPT and Perplexity when they answer questions in your space. SEO targets a ranked list of links; GEO targets a written answer with a handful of sources. The underlying work overlaps heavily: clean structure, valid structured data, pages that state facts plainly. A site that is technically sound for Google is most of the way there for AI assistants.

faq.q: How long does technical SEO take to show results?
faq.a: Technical SEO fixes ship in weeks, but Google recrawls and re-evaluates on its own schedule, so movement typically shows over the following weeks to months. Anyone promising a specific position by a specific date is guessing. What appears quickly is the mechanical evidence: pages moving from discovered to indexed, rich results showing up, Core Web Vitals passing.

faq.q: Can you guarantee a first page ranking on Google?
faq.a: No, and no honest vendor can guarantee a first page ranking on Google, because ranking is Google's decision, not ours. What we control is everything on your side of the line: whether pages get crawled, how fast they load, whether structured data is present and valid, whether content is structured so it can be quoted. We fix those and show you the before and after.

faq.q: Do I need a new website, or can you fix my existing one?
faq.a: Usually the existing site is fixable. Most problems, missing markup, slow pages, broken redirects, client-only rendering, can be repaired in the codebase you already have, whether that is Next.js, WordPress, Shopify or WooCommerce. We only recommend a rebuild when the platform itself blocks the fix, and we will say so in writing during the audit.
